newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary attracted more tourists in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Hungary attracted more tourists in Q1.

text.p: The number of tourists visiting Hungary rose by 4.8 percent in the first half of the year compared to the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (KSH) said.
Hotel occupancy rates rose 2.6 percent to 41.8 percent despite a 20 percent nominal rise in prices, it added.
The average price of a two-bed hotel room with bathroom was almost 10,000 forints ($53) per night in May, KSH said.
Revenues from tourism are important for Hungary to keep its current account deficit at levels around $2 billion.
Analysts said earlier on Monday that tourism revenues improved the current account in the Jan-April period and the country was likely to boost them further during the summer.

National Bank of Hungary current account figures published earlier on Tuesday showed that tourist revenues rose to $281 million in the January-April period from $194 million in the same period of last year.
